bullets.title: NVDA: Jensen Huang resigns as CEO — consensus PT cuts, governance risk premium widens
bullets.body: Jensen Huang resigned as NVIDIA President, CEO, and board member effective immediately following reports of an undisclosed personal relationship and DOJ antitrust probes (into NVDA-Groq deal, RunAI acquisition, and Megaspeed). CFO Colette Kress named Interim CEO; Harvey Jones appointed first-ever board Chair. PT cuts across the street: Citi to $225 (from $285), JPM to $215, KeyBanc fair value $150 (10x FY28E EPS $15.54), DA Davidson to $200 (from $300). Stock hit 52-week low of ~$155-161, down 7-10% on the day. Q3 results still scheduled for Nov 17, with consensus revenue ~$109B. Analysts flagging China/Southeast Asia export control risk (~8-10% EPS impact), succession uncertainty (Ian Buck leads odds at 37%), and broader AI capex confidence risk.

bullets.title: NVDA: DOJ pursuing multiple antitrust probes; Alice Huang/DeepSeek connection adds complexity
bullets.body: DOJ is directly probing NVIDIA on antitrust grounds, and separately investigating SMCI and Megaspeed with focus on Alice Huang's involvement; Commerce Department's Megaspeed investigation was transferred to DOJ after NVIDIA's GC inquired about it. Additionally, Alice Huang-related companies invested in DeepSeek, which was reportedly promising NVIDIA Blackwell chips to investors.

bullets.title: NVDA: HF dip-buyers active; rotation into AMD/AVGO/ANET flagged post-Huang exit
bullets.body: Oppenheimer desk notes hedge fund buyers active on NVDA dip with stock recovering from lows. At semis roundtable, AMD voted #1 new money buy idea post-NVDA news; ANET had 50%+ Buy sentiment pre-news; AVGO positioned as heir apparent for AI chip capital allocation. MRVL seen as mixed — hurt by NVDA relationship risks but helped by custom silicon market expansion.

bullets.title: NBIS: Citi upgrades to Buy, $265 PT on strong Q3 beat and 2027 profitability path
bullets.body: Nebius Q3 revenue $981M beat consensus by 9%, up 571% Y/Y; ARR $6.4B ahead by 18%. GPU-hour pricing up >20% QoQ; new contracts >$25M ACV/MW. 2027 revenue guided $12-13B (4x growth), pre-tax breakeven by Q4 2027; 2027 capex $40-45B with 75-85% funded by prepayments. Citi upgrades to Buy with $265 PT (71% upside), flagging High Risk on MSFT+META concentration (~40% of FY26 ARR). Stock was down ~19% in pre-market on initial read of guidance cut before full context.

bullets.title: HUBS: Co-founder Halligan returns as CEO; stock +8-10% on leadership overhaul
bullets.body: Brian Halligan returns as CEO effective Nov 12, replacing Yamini Rangan, in what he calls a 'refounding.' CFO Kate Bueker retiring Feb 2027; Karen Burgess (Adobe Creativity & Productivity CFO) joins as EVP Finance Nov 30, then CFO Feb 1. HUBS reaffirmed Q4/FY26 guidance. KeyBanc (Sector Weight) expects deeper headcount cuts beyond the summer's 7% layoff and M&A acceleration. Wolfe (Peer Perform) models FY27/28 growth at 10%/8% vs consensus 11%/11%, with fair value $150-$260; waiting on agent monetization inflection. Stock trades at 2.4x CY27 EV/revenue vs sector 5.7x.

bullets.title: CRWV: +25% on $132.5B backlog beat; raising $4B investment-grade debt
bullets.body: CoreWeave surged ~25% on earnings beat/raise with $132.5B backlog driving AI trade rebound. Separately raising at least $4B in investment-grade debt backed by customer contracts; Citi notes the debt tender could accrete ~$27/sh equity value through YE27. Stock was down 14.4% pre-market in sympathy with NVDA before the reversal.

bullets.title: CSCO: F1Q revenue ~$18.3-18.4B (+23% y/y); raises FY27 guide, AI revenue target to $8B
bullets.body: Cisco expects F1Q revenue ~$18.3-18.4B, up ~23% y/y, with FY27 guidance raised to ~$73.25B. AI revenue target raised to $8B. Reports tonight alongside AMAT (F1Q27 revenue guidance ~$11.0B).

bullets.title: INTU: Mixed funnel checks ahead of earnings; P/E 16.1x below SPX at 18.3x
bullets.body: Citi notes INTU maintains FY27 9-10% revenue growth guide but flags mixed funnel checks. At 16.1x forward P/E vs SPX 18.3x, valuation appears undemanding. INTU earnings are in the upcoming calendar.

bullets.title: ESTC: Citi raises PT to $132 from $128; expects strong FQ2 print with subs acceleration
bullets.body: Citi raises ESTC PT to $132 from $128, expecting a strong FQ2 print with sales-led subscription acceleration toward 20% growth. ElevenLabs expansion into the application layer seen as constructive for infrastructure vendors including ESTC.

bullets.title: NOW: Pivoting to AI consumption and outcome-based pricing; >50% of Q3 revenue non-seat
bullets.body: At BMO conference, ServiceNow highlighted Employee Works and autonomous finance workflows as near-term growth drivers, with more than half of Q3 revenue now non-seat-based. Pricing shifting toward proof-of-value and usage-based models. Rising competition from AI-native vendors; ServiceNow's differentiation rests on enterprise governance and CMDB data layer.

bullets.title: DIS: Evercore sees double-digit FY27 growth, Avengers: Doomsday, and DTC personalization as catalysts
bullets.body: Evercore ISI previews Disney Q4 (Nov 17) earnings, flagging Disney+/Hulu app personalization under new CEO Josh D'Amaro as near-term catalyst. Deep content slate (Avengers: Doomsday) and restructuring benefits expected to drive double-digit FY27 growth with possible FY28 acceleration.

bullets.title: WYNN/LVS/MGM: UBS cuts Macau estimates and PTs across the board
bullets.body: UBS lowers 2026 Macau GGR -2% to $30.4B (flat YoY) and 2027 by -8% to $29.4B (-3% YoY), citing soft Chinese macro, offshore tax enforcement, and challenging base effects. WYNN PT cut to $124 from $136 (Buy reiterated); LVS to $48 from $56 (Neutral); MGM to $36 from $46 (Neutral). Q4 2026 GGR growth forecast at -10% YoY.

bullets.title: MSFT: Ignite preview — AI monetization, Copilot evolution, custom silicon in focus Nov 17-20
bullets.body: Citi and JPM flag Microsoft Ignite (Nov 17-20, SF) as next near-term catalyst, with investors focused on AI monetization updates, Copilot roadmap, and custom silicon progress. MSFT cybersecurity described as ~$30B franchise. MSFT also reiterated commitment to self-fund data center infrastructure without government subsidies.

bullets.title: RBLX: Optimizing for long-term retention; RBLX Build gaining traction with AI-generated games
bullets.body: Citi notes Roblox is shifting focus toward long-term user retention over near-term monetization. RBLX Build is seeing early traction enabling AI-generated game content. Agentic commerce reaching inflection across platforms.

bullets.title: FWONK/TKO: MS names FWONK a Non-AI Best Idea; LYV Investor Day shows 2031 AOI ~6% above consensus
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Sean Diffley highlights FWONK as a Non-AI Best Idea in a Nov 13 webcast, citing idiosyncratic earnings drivers. LYV Investor Day suggests 2031 AOI could reach $4.765B, ~6% above consensus.

bullets.title: SHOP: UBS hosting investor lunch Nov 18 covering agentic commerce, payments monetization, enterprise
bullets.body: UBS investor lunch on Shopify (Nov 18, NYC) will cover agentic commerce announcements, Shopify Payments pricing changes in US/Australia, enterprise opportunity sizing, and the long-term 10-year growth algorithm. Core vs. Plus revenue mix and transaction loss lapping dynamics flagged as key debate topics.

bullets.title: CHTR: Debt tender offers potential $27/sh upside through YE27
bullets.body: Citi notes CHTR's tender offer up to $1.5B could accrete ~$27/sh equity value through YE27 via purchasing debt at a discount.

bullets.title: AMZN: Agentic commerce inflection; Alexa Shopping at 400M+ users
bullets.body: Citi highlights agentic commerce reaching an inflection point, with Amazon's Alexa Shopping surpassing 400M users and META Muse scaling (though blocked by eBay and United Airlines on privacy/regulatory grounds).

bullets.title: GPU spot market softening; B300 rates revert as inference demand favors older chips
bullets.body: 1-year US rental rates for A100/H100/H200 reverted to mid-October levels over the past month; B300 rates gave back most late-October gains. Neocloud operators discounting B300 capacity to raise cash amid equity pressure. Demand shifting from training to inference, where older Nvidia accelerators are more economical. B300/GB300 clusters coming online Q4 2026–Q1 2027.

bullets.title: NVDA CEO succession odds: Ian Buck 37%, Colette Kress 26%; prediction markets active
bullets.body: Prediction markets show Ian Buck leading NVDA CEO succession at 37%, followed by Interim CEO Colette Kress at 26%. MS TMT notes internal candidates also include Jeff Fisher and Chris Malachowsky; external names floated include Jony Srouji, Rene Haas, Lisa Su, and Lip-Bu Tan. Google expected to have best AI model by year-end at 72% probability.
